note: All lines measured at 2° heading steps, powers 0.5/0.7/0.85/1, every robust shot in a run >= 3° (in practice 4°). "robust" is the better clearing line of the repo planner (__runPlan, beam 3) and a wider beam that keeps the best states per set of balls standing; `planner` says which. Lines replay exactly through window.__run.loadSpec(spec, n) then window.__runShot({deg, power}) per shot.

tables.name: Clear the Table
tables.problem: Target 200 is 29% of the robust line (700); one banked 8 pays 425 on a 6° window, so the bar is passed on the first pot.
tables.proposal: Keep the layout; raise the target.
tables.catch: Three plain pots clear the table but fall short of the bar; the 8 off a rail clears it alone.

tables.name: In Order Pays More
tables.problem: Target 250 is 30% of the in-order robust line (830). Layout is Table 1 mirrored with the 8 moved up-table. The repo planner (greedy) takes the 8 first for 425 and reports 680; the in-order sweep pays 830.
tables.proposal: Keep the layout; raise the target so the out-of-order line (725) passes narrowly and the sweep passes clearly.
tables.catch: The 8 is the fattest pot on the table, and it pays most if you leave it for last.

tables.name: Rails Add Mult
tables.problem: Lowest robust total of the first seven tables (510): rails pay less here than on Table 1 (700). The robust line pots the 8 straight (85, no rail) once the cue has moved, so the wall does not force a bank. Shares the 1/2-by-the-side-pockets motif with 5, 6, 7.
tables.proposal: Needs a redesign (8 hung by a pocket behind a wall, reachable only by a one-rail kick); the search for it was not finished. Retune only for now.
tables.catch: The 8 is behind the wall: the straight shot is gone, and the way round is the one that pays.

tables.name: Two in One Shot
tables.problem: The card says two balls in one shot pays more, but the shot is barely there: the widest window that sinks the 1 and 2 together is 2° of aim, so no line a new player can hit ever uses it. The robust line (525) pots one ball a shot.
tables.proposal: Hang the pair under the left side pocket and start the cue ball over it (spawn x −4.5). The two-in-one becomes a 9° shot at half power and 7° at any other, paying 280. The 3 goes to the far right corner and the 8 near right.
tables.catch: Four balls, four shots, but the two by the side pocket go down together for more than both apart.

tables.risk: Only partly validated: the two-in-one is now a wide shot (9° of aim, measured, paying 280) and a clearing robust line opens with it, but the best-paying robust line found still pots one ball a shot (620 against 545). The 3 and the 8 need one more search so the shot it saves is worth more. Approve the direction and I will finish that search before it ships.

tables.name: Free Shot Ring
tables.problem: Table 10 is Table 9's rack with the bumpers taken off and a ring added, so two tables in a row look the same. Five balls and five shots, with the ring off to one side of the obvious first shot.
tables.proposal: Its own rack: five balls in a loose ring round the table, with the +1 shot ring on the line to the 1. The robust line takes the ring on its second shot and clears with a shot to spare (1735, up from 1305).
tables.catch: Five balls and five shots leave no room for a miss, unless the 1 is sunk through the ring.

tables.name: Two in One, 8 Last
tables.problem: This table cannot be cleared by shots a player can rely on. Five balls in four shots needs a two-in-one, and the widest one here is 2° of aim; the best robust line leaves a ball standing (355) and costs a heart. It also reuses Table 4's pair by the side pocket.
tables.proposal: Put the pair in the near right corner, behind the cue ball, start the cue ball over it (spawn x 6.5) and set the ×2 ring between them. The opener is a 6° two-in-one through the ring that pays 360; then the 3, the 4 and the 8, one a shot, in order (2040).
tables.catch: Four shots for five balls: the pair behind you has to go down together, and the ring on the way doubles it.

targetProblem: Targets sit far below what a careful player scores, so beating the target is rarely a decision. Measured against each table's robust line (every shot with at least 3° to spare), today's targets run from 29% to 67% with no trend: Table 1 asks for 200 where the robust line makes 700, and one banked 8 alone pays 425. On Table 13 a single unused shot pays 650 against a target of 625. On 7 of the 13 tables one good pot or one spare shot already clears the bar.
targetRule: Set each target from its table's measured robust total: 40% of it on Table 1, rising 3.5 points a table to 82% on Table 13, rounded to 25. Early tables stay forgiving; by the end the target takes most of a clean line. Re-measure and re-apply whenever a layout, shot count or scoring rule changes.

checks.aimRun: 100% agree on the three proposed layouts (tables 4, 10, 12; 810 lines drawn and played with the layouts swapped into tables.json), and 100% on all 13 as authored (3,510 lines)
